source.title: Skin-Deep: A Geometric Diagnostic for Alignment Fragility in Large Language Model Representations
source.authors: D. Lee; Jungseob Lee; Seungyoon Lee; Seongtae Hong; Suhyune Son; Sugyeong Eo; Jaehyung Seo; Heuiseok Lim

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance, using rank-eight LoRA on harmless Alpaca subsets and a different evaluation protocol from the original sources.
record.gate_note: The paper reports benign LoRA fine-tuning trajectories for harmful compliance, so those results bear directly on V2. It also reports refusal changes after residual-stream direction ablation; these are related to localized representation directions, but do not test whether safety is carried by a small set of weights or ranks. The token-position table measures activation separation, not aligned-versus-base per-token KL. Other geometric and cross-model results do not directly measure a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: Measures harmful compliance on 50 held-out harmful prompts after rank-8 LoRA fine-tuning on harmless Alpaca subsets (n=5–200) across seven instruction-tuned models (Table 10, Fig. 3). This bears directly on V2. The method and judge (harm-string match plus Llama-Guard) differ from the originals. Direction ablations act on residual-stream activations, not weights or ranks, so they do not test V5. Table 3 measures prompt-token activation separation, not aligned-vs-base per-token KL over response positions, so it does not test V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also stress that the GFS–compliance link is an endpoint association among initially safe models, not a calibrated forecast across attacks, update sizes or recipes.
record.recipe_differences: Tests benign-data fine-tuning with rank-eight LoRA on harmless Alpaca subsets and measures harmful compliance on 50 held-out prompts. It is not a controlled comparison of fine-tuning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with model and training-set size. Gemma-2-9B has a non-monotonic trajectory and a lower endpoint rate than the other models. The authors also caution that extraction and behavioral protocols affect the measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating selected residual-stream directions (PCA-PC1, cPCA-PC1, Arditi) at a peak layer markedly lowers harmful-request refusal in 4 of 6 models. The effective direction differs by model. Random directions leave refusal near baseline, and PCA-PC4 raises Llama refusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal depends on model-specific low-dimensional activation directions (representation-level localization, distinct from weight/rank localization).

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful/benign prompt separation along cPCA directions is weak at the first prompt token (|d|≤0.27) but strong at the final and mean-pooled tokens (Table 3). This concerns prompt positions, not response-token KL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-level safety separation of prompts accumulates across prompt tokens rather than appearing at the first token.

record.problems: The LoRA evidence uses one benign-data fine-tuning protocol and a small, heterogeneous model cohort. Added models and some Gemma entries lack multi-seed uncertainty estimates. Harmful compliance is measured using a rule-based harm-string match together with Llama-Guard; the paper notes that refusal and compliance protocols are not complements. The study does not establish a calibrated forecast across attacks, update sizes, or training recipes.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row cap was reached after all 49 reported LoRA model-by-size conditions and 11 selected direction-ablation conditions. Other directions and ablation conditions in Tables 4 and 9 were omitted. Table 3's token-position activation-separation values and other geometry results were not entered as rows because they do not measure the listed claim versions; notably, Table 3 is not a per-token KL measurement.

untested.parts: Only rank-8 LoRA on harmless Alpaca subsets is tested. Full-parameter fine-tuning, other benign datasets (e.g. Dolly, identity-shift), selected benign data and larger models (>14B) are untested. No capability check is reported.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models over response positions.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No weight or rank localization; only activation-direction ablation.
Not tested. The DPO-ordering discussion is a hypothesis about GFS, not a test of what causes shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: R37 and R44 values were corrected after reading Table 10 column-wise; the core-model block confirms this layout. The Mistral rows (baseline 0.84) are left as 'partial' per the reader, but the gain is ceiling-limited rather than weak. The compliance judge (harm-string match plus Llama-Guard) differs from the originals' GPT-4 harmfulness judge. The study is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: Only rank-eight LoRA fine-tuning on harmless Alpaca subsets is tested; other benign datasets, fine-tuning recipes, and model populations are not tested.
The study does not measure per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant-prefix prefill, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes are not tested.
The study ablates residual-stream activation directions, not weights or ranks; it does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety.
The study does not establish what data or training objective produces shallow safety.
It does not train to deepen safety or test whether deepened safety holds up.
